purpose: Add a `callisto matrix` CLI subcommand that reads napi-rs and maturin native build target declarations plus npm/PyPI runtime-version constraints from workspace manifests, and emits a deterministic, structured MatrixReport (JSON or human-readable table) that CI workflows consume as the source of truth for build matrices, eliminating hand-maintained YAML drift.
scope: New `callisto matrix [--package <name>]` CLI subcommand, reusing the existing global `--format text|json` flag (crates/callisto-cli/src/cli.rs GlobalArgs.format, OutputFormat::{Text,Json}) exactly as every other subcommand does (see crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/status.rs:41 `match global.format`) -- MatrixArgs declares no `--format` field of its own. `OutputFormat::Text` renders the human-readable table; `OutputFormat::Json` renders the MatrixReport JSON. This resolves a collision the original design doc's illustrative `--format json|table` syntax would have caused: `format` is `global = true` in GlobalArgs, so a subcommand-local `--format` with different variants cannot coexist with it. (crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/matrix.rs, wired into crates/callisto-cli/src/cli.rs `Command::Matrix`). `crates/callisto-graph/src/matrix.rs` contains the manifest-reading and MatrixReport-assembly logic (private helpers); `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/matrix.rs` contains the public `pub fn matrix<R: CommandRunner, D: DependencyResolver>(ws: &Workspace<'_, R, D>, opts: &MatrixOptions) -> Result<MatrixReport, GraphError>` entry point that calls into matrix.rs, mirroring the commands/publish.rs -> apply.rs/groups.rs pattern (both files exist; matrix.rs is not the public entry point). The private matrix.rs module: (1) reads napi.targets from package.json via a NEW read-only path in matrix.rs -- NOT via NapiTargetsIndex::load (crates/callisto-graph/src/napi.rs). NapiTargetsIndex::load is unsuitable for two independent, verified reasons: its `.and_then(|t| t.as_array())` at napi.rs:54 silently coerces a non-array `napi.targets` value to "absent" rather than surfacing an error, which would make AC-010c (malformed-type error case) unimplementable through it; and it is keyed by `GroupName` over `groups.fixed` only (napi.rs:29), not by registered package, which does not match matrix's per-package iteration model. matrix.rs's independent read still calls the existing `triple_to_role` to validate triple recognition and derive platform/arch/abi from the returned `ManifestRole::Platform`, satisfying AC-001/AC-002's "reuse triple_to_role, do not duplicate the table" requirement -- only the manifest-field READ is new code, not the triple-to-attributes MAPPING. WITHOUT modifying napi.rs; (2) reads `[tool.maturin].targets` from pyproject.toml (new read path in crates/callisto-manifests/src/python.rs or a narrowly-scoped read inside matrix.rs if adding it to python.rs is out of proportion -- implementer's call, but the triple recognition MUST reuse `triple_to_role`, not a second table); (3) reads `engines.node` from package.json and `requires-python` from pyproject.toml as raw strings; (4) derives hostRunner/useCross for each recognised triple via a NEW per-triple lookup table in matrix.rs, keyed on triple alone (keyed on the exact triple strings `triple_to_role` actually recognises today: `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl`, `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`, `i686-pc-windows-msvc`, `aarch64-pc-windows-msvc`, `armv7-unknown-linux-gnueabihf`, `x86_64-unknown-freebsd`, `aarch64-linux-android`, `armv7-linux-androideabi`, `riscv64gc-unknown-linux-gnu`, `powerpc64le-unknown-linux-gnu`, `s390x-unknown-linux-gnu`, `wasm32-wasip1`, `wasm32-unknown-unknown` -- this list differs from the design doc's illustrative table in .claude/specs/callisto-matrix.md section 3.1, which is stale prose, not code; the code table in napi.rs is authoritative per REQ-007); artifactName is derived separately, per PlatformTarget, by a package-name-keyed formatter (package_name with every "/" replaced by "-", then platform, arch, and -- only when abi is Some -- abi; see AC-013) and is NOT part of this per-triple table, since it must vary by package even when the triple is shared across packages; (5) assembles, sorts, and serializes the MatrixReport. New public types MatrixReport, PlatformTargetGroup, PlatformTarget (no `rid` field), RuntimeVersionEntry (no `targetFrameworks`/dotnet fields) live in crates/callisto-model/src/matrix.rs (or crates/callisto-graph/src/matrix.rs if the maintainer prefers graph-layer placement -- either is acceptable provided the types derive Serialize/Deserialize and PartialEq for testability; this spec fixes the location as crates/callisto-model/src/matrix.rs for consistency with other report types such as StatusReport). Updates to .github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml to replace the existing `{"platformTargets":{}}` stub with a call to the real subcommand piped through the jq expression specified in REQ-007's done_when list. Adds DiagnosticCode::UnrecognisedPlatformTriple to crates/callisto-model/src/diagnostic.rs and a corresponding row to the diagnostic attribution table at docs/01-spec.md section G.13, per the established convention set by SPEC-002's BareRuleMatchesMultipleEcosystems addition.
non_goals: dotnet-aot target kind: no .NET RID table, no reading of <TargetFramework>/<TargetFrameworks>/<RuntimeIdentifiers> from .csproj files, no PlatformTarget.rid field, no MSBuild/XML parsing of any kind. Deferred to a follow-up track; callisto-manifests has zero .NET/XML support today.

Java (Maven/Gradle) and dotnet RuntimeVersionEntry ecosystem values ('java', 'dotnet'). The RuntimeVersionEntry.ecosystem field in this spec is a closed enum of exactly 'npm' and 'python'; adding 'java'/'dotnet' variants is follow-up work, not a forward-compatible placeholder implemented here.
The dotnet-aot dispatch block in a callisto-build-action composite action (design doc section 7.2, kind=dotnet-aot).

Creating the callisto-build-action composite action itself is optional for this spec -- the CLI subcommand and its JSON contract are the hard requirement; the composite action (napi/maturin dispatch blocks) may ship in the same cycle if time allows but its absence does not block spec completion.
YAML generation for GitHub Actions workflows beyond the single jq-piped nativeMatrix output line specified in REQ-007.
Inferring maturin targets from manylinux compat tags; the matrix reader requires explicit `[tool.maturin] targets = [...]` and does no compat-tag inference.

Fetching current LTS/version-support data from external services (Node release schedule, PyPI classifiers) to expand engines.node/requires-python ranges into discrete version lists. Ranges are emitted as raw manifest strings only, with zero HTTP calls (hermetic-by-design invariant).

Any modification to napi.rs's existing triple_to_role/role_to_triple functions, their triple table, or NapiTargetsIndex's existing drift-detection behavior. matrix.rs is a read-only consumer of triple_to_role.

Discrete version-range parsing/validation of engines.node or requires-python (e.g. semver range validation, PEP 440 validation). The range string is passed through verbatim with no syntax checking; a malformed range string is not a matrix-command error.

Support for maturin/napi packages that declare targets via mechanisms other than the exact manifest fields `napi.targets` (package.json) and `[tool.maturin].targets` (pyproject.toml) -- e.g. environment-variable-driven or Cargo.toml-embedded target lists are not read.
Caching or incremental recomputation of the matrix report across invocations; each `callisto matrix` invocation performs a full manifest walk.

api_surface.name: MatrixReport
api_surface.signature: pub struct MatrixReport { pub schema_version: u32, pub platform_targets: BTreeMap<String, PlatformTargetGroup>, pub runtime_versions: BTreeMap<String, Vec<RuntimeVersionEntry>>, #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")] pub diagnostics: Vec<Diagnostic> } // serde(rename_all = "camelCase") -> {"schemaVersion":1,"platformTargets":{...},"runtimeVersions":{...},"diagnostics":[...]}. impl Report for MatrixReport { const COMMAND = "matrix"; fn schema_version(&self) -> u32 { self.schema_version } fn diagnostics(&self) -> &[Diagnostic] { &self.diagnostics } }
api_surface.description:
Top-level report type returned by callisto_graph::commands::matrix() and serialized as the JSON output. Follows the exact StatusReport precedent (crates/callisto-model/src/report.rs:297-306): schema_version is always SCHEMA_VERSION (currently 1); diagnostics carries UnrecognisedPlatformTriple warnings (AC-011) and is omitted from JSON entirely when empty via skip_serializing_if. BTreeMap guarantees lexicographic key ordering by registered package name without a separate sort step. An empty report with no diagnostics serializes to {"schemaVersion":1,"platformTargets":{},"runtimeVersions":{}} -- no diagnostics key present. The `Report` trait impl exists for schema_version()/diagnostics() accessor consistency with StatusReport, NOT as a signal to use write_report_json -- crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/matrix.rs's Json arm calls crate::output::write_json (matching status.rs:42, NOT publish.rs's write_report_json), so no top-level "command" discriminator key is injected into the output; write_report_json is used only by publish.rs/plan_publish.rs in this codebase and StatusReport (which also implements Report) is likewise rendered via plain write_json.

Package identity and collision semantics: both map keys and PlatformTarget.package_name/RuntimeVersionEntry's owning key use PackageId::name() (the bare name string, e.g. "native-mod"), matching the established convention at crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs:82,123 (`index.bare.insert(primary_id.name().to_string(), ...)`) -- NOT PackageId::display_name() ("ecosystem/name"). This is safe because every package registered by the walker carries a PackageId::Bare identity (IgnoreWalkLocator builds ids via PackageId::parse on plain manifest names, which always yields Bare, never Prefixed -- Prefixed only appears in [[package]]/[[package-set]] CONFIG RULE patterns, never in a discovered package's own id) and the walker already rejects two packages sharing the same bare name via GraphError::DuplicatePackage at insert time (walk.rs:125-132), so name() collisions across the matrix report's map keys cannot occur. runtime_versions is BTreeMap<String, Vec<RuntimeVersionEntry>> (not a single RuntimeVersionEntry) because ONE registered package can legitimately carry BOTH an npm manifest (engines.node) and a PyPI manifest (requires-python) in the same directory (the identical dual-manifest topology AC-017 already governs for platform_targets) -- these are two real, non-conflicting runtime constraints on the same package, not a source conflict, so both entries coexist in the Vec rather than erroring.

api_surface.name: PlatformTargetGroup
api_surface.signature: pub struct PlatformTargetGroup { pub kind: PlatformTargetKind, pub source: String, pub targets: Vec<PlatformTarget> } ; pub enum PlatformTargetKind { Napi, Maturin } // serde(rename_all = "lowercase") -> "napi" | "maturin"
api_surface.description: One package's native-build target group. `source` is the raw manifest field name ('napi.targets' or '[tool.maturin].targets'), used for audit output only -- not a filesystem path. `targets` is sorted by triple string before serialization. PlatformTargetKind deliberately omits a DotnetAot variant; adding one is out of scope for this spec.

api_surface.name: PlatformTarget
api_surface.signature: pub struct PlatformTarget { pub triple: String, pub platform: String, pub arch: String, pub abi: Option<String>, pub host_runner: String, pub use_cross: bool, pub artifact_name: String, pub package_dir: String, pub package_name: String } // serde(rename_all = "camelCase")
api_surface.description: One platform build target within a PlatformTargetGroup. No `rid` field (napi/maturin only, no dotnet-aot). `abi` serializes as JSON null when None (darwin, freebsd, android, wasi/unknown-wasm32 targets and all win32 targets carry no abi). `triple` and derived platform/arch/abi come from callisto_graph::napi::triple_to_role; host_runner/use_cross come from a per-triple table in matrix.rs keyed on triple alone. `artifact_name` is computed separately, by a package-name-keyed formatter (package_name with every "/" replaced by "-", then platform, arch, and -- only when abi is Some -- abi; see AC-013) -- NOT a per-triple table lookup, since two packages sharing the same triple must still produce distinct artifact_name values. `package_dir` is workspace-root-relative.

api_surface.name: RuntimeVersionEntry
api_surface.signature: pub struct RuntimeVersionEntry { pub ecosystem: RuntimeEcosystem, pub field: String, pub range: String } ; pub enum RuntimeEcosystem { Npm, Python } // serde(rename_all = "lowercase") -> "npm" | "python"
api_surface.description: One package's runtime-version constraint, sourced from engines.node (npm) or requires-python (python/PyPI). `range` is the raw, unvalidated manifest string. No targetFrameworks field (dotnet-only, out of scope).

api_surface.name: callisto_graph::commands::matrix
api_surface.signature: pub fn matrix<R: CommandRunner, D: DependencyResolver>(ws: &Workspace<'_, R, D>, opts: &MatrixOptions) -> Result<MatrixReport, GraphError> ; pub struct MatrixOptions { pub package: Option<String> }
api_surface.description: Builds the MatrixReport for the workspace (or a single package when opts.package is Some). Matches the existing status()/plan_publish() signature pattern (crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/status.rs, publish.rs) -- returns GraphError, not CliError, since callisto-graph cannot name a type from callisto-cli (callisto-cli depends on callisto-graph, not the reverse). crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/matrix.rs converts GraphError to CliError via the existing From impl, exactly as the other command handlers do. Returns Err when opts.package names a package not present in the workspace's registered package set, and Err on any manifest read/parse failure (unreadable file, malformed TOML/JSON). Emits a warning-level Diagnostic with DiagnosticCode::UnrecognisedPlatformTriple (added to crates/callisto-model/src/diagnostic.rs, kebab-case serde value "unrecognised-platform-triple") per unrecognised napi/maturin triple encountered and excludes that triple from targets[] without failing the call. When a single registered package declares BOTH napi.targets and [tool.maturin].targets, matrix() returns Err(GraphError::ConflictingPlatformTargetSources { package: PackageId, napi_source: &'static str, maturin_source: &'static str }) -- code E118, #[error("package `{package}` declares platform targets via both `{napi_source}` and `{maturin_source}`; only one source is allowed")], #[diagnostic(code(E118), help("Remove one of the two target declarations -- either napi.targets in package.json or [tool.maturin].targets in pyproject.toml -- from the package's manifest."))], matching the field-list/diagnostic-code/help-text shape established by E117 UnexpectedManifestVersion in crates/callisto-graph/src/error.rs. This is a hard error, not a silent last-write-wins or dual-key split.

api_surface.name: callisto matrix (CLI subcommand)
api_surface.description: New Command::Matrix(MatrixArgs) variant in crates/callisto-cli/src/cli.rs and handler in crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/matrix.rs. Uses the existing global `--format text|json` flag exactly like every other subcommand (crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/status.rs:41 pattern) -- MatrixArgs has no format field of its own. `--format json` (or bare, since the global default is text -- see AC-003b) renders MatrixReport as JSON; `--format text` renders the human-readable table. --package restricts output to one registered package name. Exit code 0 on success including an empty report; exit code 1 on a manifest read/parse error. Unknown --package name is also an exit-code-1 error with a message naming the unknown package (not a silent empty report).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: In a workspace containing a group with a napi package.json declaring napi.targets = ["aarch64-apple-darwin", "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"], running `callisto matrix --format json` produces a platformTargets entry keyed by the group's registered package name, with kind:"napi", source:"napi.targets", and targets[] containing exactly 2 PlatformTarget objects whose triple/platform/arch/abi fields match the values returned by callisto_graph::napi::triple_to_role for each of those two triples.

In a workspace containing a pyproject.toml with [tool.maturin].targets = ["x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu", "aarch64-apple-darwin"], running `callisto matrix --format json` produces a platformTargets entry with kind:"maturin", source:"[tool.maturin].targets", and targets[] whose platform/arch/abi/hostRunner/useCross values for each triple are identical to the values produced for the same triple string in a napi group in AC-001 -- i.e. the triple-to-platform-attributes derivation is provably shared code, not a duplicated table.

In a workspace with no napi.targets fields, no [tool.maturin].targets fields, no engines.node fields, and no requires-python fields anywhere, running `callisto matrix --format json` prints pretty-printed JSON to stdout (via crate::output::write_json, matching status.rs:42 -- NOT write_report_json, so no top-level "command" key is injected) that parses to a value deeply equal to {"schemaVersion":1,"platformTargets":{},"runtimeVersions":{}}, with no "diagnostics" key present (skip_serializing_if on the empty Vec), and the process exits with code 0.

Running bare `callisto matrix` with no --format flag at all uses the global default (OutputFormat::Text, crates/callisto-cli/src/cli.rs GlobalArgs.format default_value = "text") and renders the human-readable table, not JSON -- identical behavior to `callisto matrix --format text`. This matches every other subcommand's no-flag default.

In a workspace with an npm package whose package.json contains "engines": {"node": ">=20.0.0"} and no pyproject.toml, running `callisto matrix --format json` produces a runtimeVersions entry for that package's registered name (PackageId::name()) equal to an array containing exactly one element: {"ecosystem":"npm","field":"engines.node","range":">=20.0.0"}.

In a workspace with a PyPI package whose pyproject.toml contains requires-python = ">=3.9" and no package.json, running `callisto matrix --format json` produces a runtimeVersions entry for that package's registered name (PackageId::name()) equal to an array containing exactly one element: {"ecosystem":"python","field":"requires-python","range":">=3.9"}.

In a workspace where a single registered package's directory contains both a package.json with "engines": {"node": ">=20.0.0"} and a pyproject.toml with requires-python = ">=3.9", running `callisto matrix --format json` produces a runtimeVersions entry for that package's registered name equal to an array containing exactly two elements, {"ecosystem":"npm","field":"engines.node","range":">=20.0.0"} and {"ecosystem":"python","field":"requires-python","range":">=3.9"} in that order (npm before python, matching RuntimeEcosystem's declared variant order) -- this is not an error; both real runtime constraints on the same package coexist.

In a workspace with two or more napi/maturin/runtime-version-bearing packages, running `callisto matrix --package <name> --format json` where <name> is exactly one package's PackageId::name() string produces a report containing only that package's entries in platformTargets and runtimeVersions (all other packages' keys absent from both maps). --package matches against the same PackageId::name() string used as the map keys (see api_surface's package identity note) -- not display_name() and not a partial/glob match.

Running `callisto matrix --package does-not-exist --format json` in any workspace exits with code 1 and prints a human-readable error message that names "does-not-exist" as an unrecognised package (no PackageId::name() in the workspace's registered package set matches it); it does not print a structurally valid empty MatrixReport.

Running `callisto matrix --format text` in a workspace with at least one napi target and one runtime-version entry produces non-JSON, human-readable ASCII table output on stdout and exits 0; the table's column layout is not asserted to be stable across releases (no snapshot test pins its exact byte content beyond confirming it is non-empty and non-JSON).

In a workspace with three or more packages producing platformTargets entries, the keys of the platformTargets object in --format json output (each key being the exact PackageId::name() string) appear in strict lexicographic order, and the keys of runtimeVersions likewise; within a single PlatformTargetGroup with two or more targets, the targets[] array is ordered by ascending triple string; within a runtimeVersions entry with two elements (AC-005b), the array is ordered npm before python.

Running `callisto matrix --format json` against a workspace containing a REGISTERED package (i.e. its directory also has a valid, name-bearing package.json OR is otherwise discoverable by the workspace locator -- see note below) whose pyproject.toml has malformed TOML syntax (e.g. an unterminated string) exits with code 1 and prints an error identifying the unreadable/malformed manifest path; no MatrixReport JSON is printed to stdout. NOTE on registration: crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/ignore_walk.rs silently drops a directory's pyproject.toml from package discovery entirely when it fails to parse (`if let Ok(doc) = content.parse::<toml_edit::DocumentMut>()` -- no error path), so a directory whose ONLY manifest is a malformed pyproject.toml registers NO package at all and matrix() -- which iterates only already-registered packages -- never reads that file. This criterion therefore requires the malformed pyproject.toml to sit in a directory that is ALSO registered via a valid package.json (matrix.rs's own read of pyproject.toml, independent of the locator's silent-drop, is what surfaces the parse error for an already-registered package).

Running `callisto matrix --format json` against a workspace containing a REGISTERED package whose package.json has malformed JSON syntax (e.g. a trailing comma) exits with code 1 and prints an error identifying the unreadable/malformed manifest path; no MatrixReport JSON is printed to stdout. Mirrors AC-010 for the JSON-manifest side of the same read pass, with the same registration caveat: a malformed package.json with no valid "name" field is silently dropped by the locator (crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/ignore_walk.rs's `if let Ok(val) = serde_json::from_str(...)` has no error path), so this criterion requires the package to be registered via SOME valid manifest (e.g. a co-located Cargo.toml, or the malformed package.json sitting alongside a valid pyproject.toml) so matrix() reaches it and re-reads the malformed package.json directly.

Running `callisto matrix --format json` against a workspace where a package.json's napi.targets array contains a triple not recognised by callisto_graph::napi::triple_to_role (e.g. "sparc64-unknown-linux-gnu") exits 0, the MatrixReport's diagnostics[] array contains exactly one Diagnostic with code DiagnosticCode::UnrecognisedPlatformTriple identifying the unrecognised triple and the offending package (via the Diagnostic's package/message fields), and that triple is excluded from targets[] while any other recognised triples from the same or other packages remain in the report. Under --format text, the same diagnostic is rendered in the human-readable table output.

For each of the 18 triples callisto_graph::napi::triple_to_role recognises, every PlatformTarget produced for that triple has exactly the following hostRunner and useCross values (matching the design doc's per-platform-family rule at .claude/specs/callisto-matrix.md section 3.1, corrected for the triples that actually exist in code): aarch64-apple-darwin -> ("macos-latest", false); x86_64-apple-darwin -> ("macos-13", false); x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -> ("ubuntu-latest", false); x86_64-unknown-linux-musl -> ("ubuntu-latest", true); aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu -> ("ubuntu-latest", true); aarch64-unknown-linux-musl -> ("ubuntu-latest", true); x86_64-pc-windows-msvc -> ("windows-latest", false); i686-pc-windows-msvc -> ("windows-latest", false); aarch64-pc-windows-msvc -> ("windows-latest", false); armv7-unknown-linux-gnueabihf -> ("ubuntu-latest", true); x86_64-unknown-freebsd -> ("ubuntu-latest", true); aarch64-linux-android -> ("ubuntu-latest", true); armv7-linux-androideabi -> ("ubuntu-latest", true); riscv64gc-unknown-linux-gnu -> ("ubuntu-latest", true); powerpc64le-unknown-linux-gnu -> ("ubuntu-latest", true); s390x-unknown-linux-gnu -> ("ubuntu-latest", true); wasm32-wasip1 -> ("ubuntu-latest", false); wasm32-unknown-unknown -> ("ubuntu-latest", false). This table is implemented as a table-driven unit test asserting all 18 pairs in one test function.

For every PlatformTarget produced by callisto matrix, artifactName equals the package's registered name (PackageId::name()) with every "/" character replaced by "-", followed by "-", the platform field, "-", the arch field, and, only when abi is Some, another "-" followed by the abi value; when abi is None the abi segment and its preceding "-" are omitted entirely. E.g. package "native-mod" on triple "aarch64-apple-darwin" (platform "darwin", arch "arm64", abi None) produces artifactName "native-mod-darwin-arm64"; scoped package "@scope/addon" on the same triple produces artifactName "@scope-addon-darwin-arm64" (the "/" in the scope is replaced, no other character is altered); package "native-mod" on triple "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu" (platform "linux", arch "x64", abi Some("gnu")) produces artifactName "native-mod-linux-x64-gnu". artifactName is not derived from the triple string at all.

For every PlatformTarget whose platform is one of darwin, freebsd, android, or wasi/unknown-with-wasm32-arch, the JSON output's abi field is null (not the string "null", not omitted); for win32-platform targets the abi field is likewise null (never "msvc"); for linux-platform targets abi is a non-null string matching the abi derived from triple_to_role's ManifestRole::Platform for that triple.

The compiled MatrixReport, PlatformTargetGroup, PlatformTarget, and RuntimeVersionEntry Rust types contain no field named `rid` and no field named `targetFrameworks`/`target_frameworks`; PlatformTargetKind has exactly two variants (napi, maturin) and RuntimeEcosystem has exactly two variants (npm, python) -- verified by attempting to deserialize {"kind":"dotnet-aot", ...} and {"ecosystem":"dotnet", ...} fixtures and asserting deserialization fails.

After this change, .github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml no longer contains the literal fallback string '{"platformTargets":{}}' as the nativeMatrix source. The NATIVE_MATRIX assignment line's jq filter argument is byte-for-byte the program `[.platformTargets[].targets[]] | unique_by(.artifactName)` (whitespace-insensitive); the surrounding shell wrapper (variable name, quoting style, additional pipeline stages) may differ from REQ-007's illustrative snippet, but the jq filter text itself must not.

In a workspace where a single registered package has both a napi.targets declaration in its package.json and a [tool.maturin].targets declaration in its pyproject.toml, running `callisto matrix --format json` exits with code 1 via Err(GraphError::ConflictingPlatformTargetSources { package, napi_source: "napi.targets", maturin_source: "[tool.maturin].targets" }) (diagnostic code E118), prints an error naming that package's registered name and both source field names, and prints no MatrixReport JSON to stdout. This is a hard error, never a silent last-write-wins or an implicit dual-key split.

Running `callisto matrix --format json` against a workspace where a package.json's napi.targets field is present but is not a JSON array of strings (e.g. {"napi":{"targets":"aarch64-apple-darwin"}} -- a bare string, not an array) exits with code 1 and prints an error identifying the package and the malformed field; no MatrixReport JSON is printed. The same rule applies to a [tool.maturin].targets value that is present but not an array (e.g. a bare string or table), and to an engines.node or requires-python value that is present but not a string (e.g. a number or object).

A package.json declaring napi.targets = [] (present, explicitly empty array) produces a platformTargets entry for that package with kind:"napi", source:"napi.targets", targets: [] -- the entry is present because the field was declared, distinguishable in the output from a package with no napi.targets field at all (which produces no platformTargets entry for that package, per AC-003).

DiagnosticCode::UnrecognisedPlatformTriple serializes to the exact kebab-case string "unrecognised-platform-triple" and deserializes back to the same variant (round-trip), mirroring the existing test pattern for DiagnosticCode::BareRuleMatchesMultipleEcosystems in crates/callisto-model/src/diagnostic.rs. A row for this variant is added to the diagnostic attribution table at docs/01-spec.md section G.13, naming the matrix module as the emitting source.

revision_note: Corrected AC-013: the shipped artifact_name_for_package_platform (crates/callisto-graph/src/matrix.rs:49-60) never used the pre-SPEC-002 "native-" + triple format this criterion described. SPEC-002 changed artifactName to {package_name ("/" -> "-")}-{platform}-{arch}[-{abi}] to fix a real collision (two packages sharing a triple produced identical artifactName under the old format) and a real sanitization bug (npm scoped package names contain "/", forbidden by actions/upload-artifact). AC-013 is rewritten to describe this actual, currently-shipped format, verified by reading matrix.rs directly. AC-012 and AC-014 were checked and do not reference artifactName or depend on the stale format (they cover hostRunner/useCross and the abi field respectively), so they are unchanged.
reasoning:
Key discovery during drafting: the design doc's section 3.1 triple table (.claude/specs/callisto-matrix.md) is NOT byte-identical to the actual triple_to_role match arms in crates/callisto-graph/src/napi.rs today. The doc lists wasm32-wasi and armv7-unknown-linux-musleabihf; the code recognises wasm32-wasip1 and wasm32-unknown-unknown instead, and has no musleabihf arm variant. Since REQ-007 explicitly mandates reusing triple_to_role and NOT duplicating the table, I anchored the spec's authoritative triple list on the actual code (verified by reading napi.rs directly) rather than the stale doc prose, and called this out explicitly in scope and AC-012 so the implementer builds the hostRunner/useCross/artifactName table against the real 18 triples, not the doc's list. Also discovered: triple_to_role's ManifestRole::Platform only carries platform/arch/abi -- it has no concept of hostRunner/useCross/artifactName, so that mapping is unavoidably NEW code in matrix.rs, keyed by triple, not an extension of napi.rs (consistent with the non-goal 'no modification to napi.rs'). Also discovered: callisto-manifests has no existing reader for [tool.maturin].targets or engines.node — python.rs only parses requires-python for a different purpose (Poetry 2.x project table) — so both are new manifest-reading code, called out in scope. Placed MatrixReport/PlatformTargetGroup/PlatformTarget/RuntimeVersionEntry in callisto-model (following the StatusReport precedent) but noted graph-layer placement is an acceptable alternative since this is an implementation/module-boundary decision, not a contract decision — the JSON shape and field names are what's load-bearing for AC purposes, not the crate they live in. Kept the composite-action (section 7 of design doc) optional per REQ-007's explicit 'nice-to-have if time allows' language, but made the action.yml wiring change (section 6.1 jq pipeline) a hard AC since REQ-007 lists it as a done_when item, not a nice-to-have.

Fixes applied from canon-auditor round 1: (1) matrix()'s signature corrected from a non-compiling `Result<MatrixReport, CliError>` (callisto-graph cannot name CliError -- wrong dependency direction) and a bare `&Workspace` (missing required lifetime/generics) to match the real status()/plan_publish() pattern: `pub fn matrix<R: CommandRunner, D: DependencyResolver>(ws: &Workspace<'_, R, D>, opts: &MatrixOptions) -> Result<MatrixReport, GraphError>`, verified against crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/status.rs:59-62. (2) Added AC-010b covering malformed package.json (JSON) parse failure, mirroring AC-010's TOML case -- the original spec only covered the TOML side of a dual-format read pass. (3) Added AC-017 specifying that a package declaring both napi.targets and [tool.maturin].targets is a hard GraphError, not undefined behavior -- api_surface updated to name the new GraphError::ConflictingPlatformTargetSources variant. (4) Fixed the previously-unpinned 'DiagnosticCode::UnrecognisedPlatformTriple or equivalent' to an exact variant name with a pinned kebab-case serde string, added AC-018 asserting the serialization round-trip and requiring a docs/01-spec.md G.13 table row, matching the established convention SPEC-002 set for BareRuleMatchesMultipleEcosystems. (5) AC-016 tightened from an ambiguous 'or an equivalent shell pipeline' to a precise byte-for-byte (whitespace-insensitive) jq-filter-text requirement, leaving only the shell wrapper's cosmetic details unconstrained. (6) Scope clarified: crates/callisto-graph/src/matrix.rs holds private read/assembly logic; crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/matrix.rs holds the public entry point -- both files exist, matching the commands/publish.rs -> apply.rs/groups.rs precedent, resolving the prior ambiguity about whether one or two files were intended.

Fixes applied from canon-auditor round 2: (1) AC-017's GraphError::ConflictingPlatformTargetSources was underspecified ('..' field list, no code/help text) -- pinned to an exact field list (package, napi_source, maturin_source), diagnostic code E118 (next available after E117 UnexpectedManifestVersion), and #[error(...)]/#[diagnostic(help(...))] text matching the shape of every other recent GraphError variant in crates/callisto-graph/src/error.rs. (2) Added AC-010c covering schema-valid-but-wrong-type manifest fields (napi.targets present as a non-array, [tool.maturin].targets present as a non-array, engines.node/requires-python present as a non-string) -- AC-010/AC-010b only covered syntax errors, not type/schema violations on an otherwise-parseable manifest. (3) Added AC-001b specifying that an explicitly-empty napi.targets = [] produces a present-but-empty platformTargets entry, distinguishable from the field being entirely absent (AC-003) -- previously undefined which of two valid interpretations applied. (4) AC-011's is_error_case corrected from true to false: it is a warning-only, exit-0 success path (the call succeeds, other targets still populate the report), unlike every other is_error_case:true criterion in this spec (AC-007, AC-010, AC-010b, AC-010c, AC-017), which all fail with a non-zero exit code -- the field now consistently means 'the CLI process exits non-zero' across all criteria that assert it true.

Fixes applied from canon-exit-gate round 3 (blocking): (1) --format json|table was unbuildable: crates/callisto-cli/src/cli.rs GlobalArgs.format is global=true over OutputFormat::{Text,Json} (no Table variant, default_value="text"), and a global clap arg cannot be shadowed by a same-named subcommand arg. Resolved by dropping the subcommand-local --format entirely and reusing the global text|json flag exactly like every existing subcommand (verified pattern: crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/status.rs:41 `match global.format`) -- Text renders the table, Json renders MatrixReport. Added AC-003b pinning the bare-invocation (no flag) default to text/table, matching every other subcommand's no-flag behavior. AC-008 renamed from --format table to --format text. (2) AC-011's warning diagnostic had no field to live in: MatrixReport was pinned to exactly two fields and AC-003 pinned the full empty-output bytes, leaving no room for a diagnostic without contradicting AC-003. Resolved by adding schema_version and diagnostics fields to MatrixReport and implementing the Report trait, following the exact StatusReport precedent (crates/callisto-model/src/report.rs:297-317, diagnostics: Vec<Diagnostic> with #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]); AC-003 updated to the new exact empty-output bytes ({"schemaVersion":1,...}, no diagnostics key when empty); AC-011 updated to assert the diagnostic appears in diagnostics[] with DiagnosticCode::UnrecognisedPlatformTriple. (3) AC-012 let the hostRunner/useCross table be anything satisfying only 'non-empty string, boolean field' -- an implementation mapping every triple to ubuntu-latest/false would have passed all 21 criteria while producing a matrix that builds no darwin or windows artifact. Resolved by pinning the exact (hostRunner, useCross) pair for all 18 real triples, derived from the design doc's per-platform-family table (.claude/specs/callisto-matrix.md section 3.1) corrected for the two triple-name discrepancies already established (wasm32-wasip1 not wasm32-wasi; no musleabihf arm) and extended to cover wasm32-unknown-unknown (absent from the doc's table entirely; assigned ubuntu-latest/false to match its sibling wasm32-wasip1 entry, since neither wasm target requires cross-compilation tooling). (4) AC-015's is_error_case corrected from true to false: it is a compile-time/type-level deserialization assertion inside a unit test with no CLI process or exit code involved, which does not fit the round-2-established definition of is_error_case (the CLI process exits non-zero) that every other true-marked criterion (AC-007, AC-010, AC-010b, AC-010c, AC-017) satisfies.

Fixes applied from canon-exit-gate round 4 (blocking, both introduced by round 3's own fix #2): (1) AC-003 pinned compact JSON bytes ({"schemaVersion":1,...} with no whitespace), but crates/callisto-cli/src/output.rs:7-9's write_json uses serde_json::to_string_pretty -- every existing command's JSON output is pretty-printed with a trailing newline, so byte-exact compact-JSON pinning was unimplementable without deviating from all 11 existing commands. AC-003 now asserts the output PARSES to the expected value (deep equality) rather than pinning exact bytes, and explicitly names write_json (not write_report_json) as the writer so the "no top-level extra key" expectation is unambiguous. (2) The round-3-mandated Report trait impl was read as implying write_report_json (which injects a "command": "matrix" key, contradicting AC-003's exact object shape) -- but write_report_json is used by exactly two commands in this codebase (publish.rs, plan_publish.rs); StatusReport also implements Report yet status.rs uses plain write_json with no injected key. The Report impl exists solely for schema_version()/diagnostics() accessor consistency, not as a writer-selection signal. api_surface for MatrixReport and the CLI subcommand entry now state explicitly that crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/matrix.rs's Json arm calls write_json, matching status.rs:42, not write_report_json.

Fixes applied from canon-exit-gate round 5 (blocking, both instances of one unstated rule -- package identity and collision semantics -- per the gate's own recommendation to fix once rather than patch case-by-case): (1) runtime_versions was BTreeMap<String, RuntimeVersionEntry> (one entry per package key), but a single registered package's directory can legitimately contain BOTH a package.json (engines.node) and a pyproject.toml (requires-python) -- the identical dual-manifest topology AC-017 already governs for platform_targets -- so AC-004 and AC-005 contradicted each other for that package with no stated resolution. Changed runtime_versions to BTreeMap<String, Vec<RuntimeVersionEntry>>; AC-004/AC-005 restated as single-element-array assertions; added AC-005b for the dual-manifest case (both entries coexist, npm-then-python order, NOT an error -- unlike AC-017's platform-target conflict, two runtime constraints on one package are not contradictory); AC-009 extended to cover the two-element ordering rule. (2) The map-key accessor (PackageId::name() vs display_name()) was never pinned. Resolved by verifying against crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs:82,123, which already establishes name() (bare name string) as this codebase's convention for package-name-keyed maps (`index.bare.insert(primary_id.name().to_string(), ...)`); pinned matrix's keys to the same accessor. Confirmed safe because every walker-discovered package carries a PackageId::Bare identity (never Prefixed -- Prefixed is exclusive to [[package]]/[[package-set]] config-rule patterns) and the walker already rejects same-bare-name collisions via GraphError::DuplicatePackage at discovery time (walk.rs:125-132), so no display_name()-vs-name() collision scenario can actually arise for a real workspace; the fix is about removing implementer ambiguity, not resolving a real collision risk. AC-006/AC-007/AC-009 updated to state --package matches against this same name() string.

Fixes applied from vector-challenger round 1 (spec-level architectural gap surfaced during planning, not caught by 6 rounds of canon review because it requires reading the workspace LOCATOR, not just the matrix module): (1) AC-010/AC-010b assumed matrix() could observe a malformed manifest in ANY directory, but matrix() (per this spec's own architecture) iterates only already-registered packages, and crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/ignore_walk.rs silently drops a directory from package discovery entirely when its only manifest fails to parse (`if let Ok(...)` with no error arm, verified at both the package.json and pyproject.toml read sites) -- so a directory whose SOLE manifest is malformed never becomes a registered package and matrix() never reaches it, making the original AC-010/AC-010b unimplementable as stated. Both criteria are narrowed to require the malformed manifest to sit in an already-registered package's directory (registered via a co-located valid manifest of a different kind), with the exact locator behavior cited inline so the implementer does not have to rediscover it. (2) Formally recorded matrix.rs's use of an independent read path instead of NapiTargetsIndex::load in scope item (1), with the exact two reasons (silent non-array coercion at napi.rs:54; GroupName-keyed rather than package-keyed) -- this was previously only true implicitly via 'reuse triple_to_role, not a second table' but the specific alternative to NapiTargetsIndex::load was undocumented, creating spec/implementation drift risk a future canon-verifier pass would flag.
